issues.legal_issue: A trial court may be understood to have condoned delay in seeking restoration when it considers facts pleaded to explain the delay and grants restoration, even without expressly referring to the condonation request.
material_facts: The suit was dismissed for non-prosecution after the plaintiffs’ counsel failed to appear, and the plaintiffs later applied to restore it.
The restoration application set out facts both explaining the non-appearance and accounting for the delay in applying for restoration.
A separate request for condonation relied on the facts stated in the restoration application.
The trial court granted restoration after finding the cause shown sufficient, although its order did not expressly refer to the separate condonation request.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s order showed that it had considered and accepted the explanation for delay; the delay was therefore implicitly condoned.
issues.legal_principle: Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs restoration of a suit dismissed for default, and Section 5 of the Limitation Act permits condonation of delay. Where the trial court’s order shows that it accepted facts that explain the delay as well as the non-appearance, the absence of an express reference to the condonation request does not establish that the delay was left uncondoned. No earlier case is cited for this principle.

rule.if: restoration_proceeding_after_default_dismissal and delay_explained_in_restoration_application and condonation_request_relies_on_those_facts and trial_court_grants_restoration_after_accepting_the_explanation and no_express_reference_to_condonation

predicates.restoration_proceeding_after_default_dis: A party seeks restoration of a suit that was dismissed after the party failed to appear or prosecute it.
predicates.delay_explained_in_restoration_applicati: The restoration application sets out facts explaining why the application was not filed sooner.
predicates.condonation_request_relies_on_those_fact: A separate request to excuse the delay adopts or relies on the facts stated in the restoration application.
predicates.trial_court_grants_restoration_after_acc: The trial court grants restoration after finding the explanation for the relevant absence and delay sufficient.
predicates.no_express_reference_to_condonation: The trial court’s order does not expressly mention the request to excuse the delay.

issues.definition: When a restoration application and a related request to excuse delay rely on the same explanation, and the trial court grants restoration after accepting that explanation, the delay is treated as condoned even if the order does not expressly say so.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court should not set aside an order restoring a suit where the trial court considered the explanations for non-appearance and delay and committed no jurisdictional illegality or material irregularity.
material_facts: The trial court restored the suit after finding sufficient cause for restoration and delay.
The High Court set aside the restoration order because the trial court had not expressly discussed limitation.
The Supreme Court concluded that the trial court had considered the delay explanation and had not acted illegally or with material irregularity in exercising its jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering with the trial court’s restoration order in revision.
issues.legal_principle: The revisional court’s interference was unwarranted because the trial court had not exercised its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity. The restoration application arose under Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the delay issue was governed by Section 5 of the Limitation Act. No earlier case is cited.

predicates.civil_revision_against_restoration_order: A party brings a civil revision challenging an order that restored a suit dismissed for default.
predicates.trial_court_considered_the_explanations_: The trial court considered and accepted the explanations for the failure to appear and for the delay in seeking restoration.
predicates.high_court_reverses_only_for_lack_of_exp: The High Court sets aside the restoration order solely because it does not expressly discuss the delay issue.

issues.definition: If a civil revision challenges a restoration order, the trial court considered the explanations for absence and delay, and the High Court reverses only because the delay was not expressly discussed, revisional interference is not justified.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier dismissal of a restoration application for non-prosecution does not bar its consideration on the merits after that dismissal has been set aside and the application reinstated by a final order.
material_facts: The restoration application was itself dismissed for non-prosecution.
A higher court set aside that dismissal, reinstated the restoration application, and directed that it be decided on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The earlier dismissal of the restoration application for non-prosecution could not be used as a ground to reject it after it had been reinstated by a final order.
issues.legal_principle: A final order setting aside a dismissal for non-prosecution and restoring an application for determination on the merits prevents the superseded dismissal from being relied on as a bar to that determination. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this point.

predicates.restoration_application_dismissed_for_no: A court dismisses an application seeking restoration because the applicant does not appear or prosecute it.
predicates.higher_court_sets_aside_dismissal_and_re: A higher court sets aside that dismissal and restores the application for decision on its merits.
predicates.reinstatement_order_is_final: The order restoring the application is no longer open to challenge.

issues.definition: When a higher court finally sets aside a non-prosecution dismissal and reinstates the application, the earlier dismissal does not bar a decision on the application’s merits.
